title: Check why tar says a file is not a tar archive
summary: tar refuses to unpack a file that is not a real archive, for example a web page or text saved under a .tar.gz name, or a broken download. Check the file's real size and content before trying again.
error_patterns: tar: This does not look like a tar archive
gzip: stdin: not in gzip format

aliases.text: tar: this does not look like a tar archive

prerequisites: The name of the file tar could not unpack
A terminal open in the folder that contains the file

steps.explain: List the files here and look at the size of the file that tar could not unpack. A real archive is usually larger than a few bytes; a size of a few bytes or a few KB of web-page text means the download went wrong.

placeholders.name: FILE
placeholders.description: The archive file that tar could not unpack

steps.expect: A line like -rw-r--r-- 1 user user 3 ... archive.tar.gz. A size of only a few bytes means the file is almost empty.

steps.explain: Show the first lines of the file as text. If you see a web page (<!DOCTYPE html>), a 'Not Found' message or other plain sentences, the download saved a page instead of the archive.

placeholders.name: FILE
placeholders.description: The archive file that tar could not unpack

steps.expect: Readable text such as <!DOCTYPE html> or a 'Not Found' message means a web page was saved. A real .tar.gz shows unreadable symbols.

steps.explain: Read the first bytes of the file. A real gzip archive starts with the bytes 1f 8b. Plain text starts with readable character codes, so the file is not a gzip archive.

placeholders.name: FILE
placeholders.description: The archive file that tar could not unpack

steps.expect: For a text file: 68 69 0a (the letters hi and a line break). For a real gzip archive the first byte pair is 1f 8b.

alternatives.explain: Ask the file command for the real type in one word. It needs the 'file' package, which is not always installed. Expect text/plain for text, application/gzip for a real gzip archive.

steps.explain: Try to list the contents of the archive without unpacking anything. If it prints file names, the archive is real and can be unpacked. If it fails with 'gzip: stdin: not in gzip format' or 'This does not look like a tar archive', the file is not a real archive: download it again from its source.

placeholders.name: FILE
placeholders.description: The archive file that tar could not unpack

steps.expect: A real archive prints its file names, for example d/ and d/a.txt. A broken file prints 'gzip: stdin: not in gzip format' and exits with status 2.

alternatives.explain: Use this for an uncompressed .tar file (no .gz ending).

placeholders.name: FILE
placeholders.description: The archive file that tar could not unpack

verify.expect: File names are printed for a real archive. The error 'gzip: stdin: not in gzip format' means the file is not gzip data.
